_note:
CYCLE 5 — P4-PRECONDITION, re-measured before being worked. P4 is a HARNESS problem ('every tool must have a fixture that can reach its happy path, or a written statement of why one cannot exist') and it is the largest block left in the denominator: 21 of the 48 still-blocked tools.

🔴 SIX OF ITS ROWS ARE SURFACING ROWS, NOT FIXTURE ROWS. glossary_create_chapter_link 0/3, glossary_create_evidence 0/3, jobs_cancel 0/5, jobs_pause 0/5, kg_ontology_propose 0/5, registry_set_skill_enabled 0/5 — a tool that never reached the wire was never blocked by its fixture. Measured 2026-08-22 with the platform's own answerable_tools against each tool's OWN recorded prompt: ALL 21 are answerable, and answerability forces a match onto the wire whatever the hot-seed budget holds. Those rows predate cycle 1's 37 declaration widenings and were never re-measured.

FIVE MORE ARE BELOW THE OWNER'S K>=5 BAR: composition_arc_apply 3/3, composition_arc_import_analyze 3/3, glossary_create_chapter_link 0/3, glossary_create_evidence 0/3, kg_propose_edge 3/3.

And FOUR are in cycle 2's fix recall (jobs_cancel, jobs_pause, kg_propose_edge, plan_bootstrap_apply): they name a supplier in a required argument, so the refusal-arming shipped in db4ab33c8/4f6c30ff8 reaches them without anything further being written for this problem.

So the first required action here is a re-measure, not a fixture campaign — the honest size of this problem is unknown until the 21 are run again at K=5 with the surface captured. Scenarios are carried over UNEDITED from their original batches.

seed_assert.why:
EIGHTY-FOUR system/unlisted motifs already exist, so there is genuinely something to adopt and the model must FIND one — composition_motif_book_list / a motif search is the supplier. Read from the store rather than assumed. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with batch 15's arc templates: the system arc-template library is EMPTY, so this is the first tool in the loop whose cross-tenancy source actually has rows.

🔴 status='active' ADDED 2026-08-23 by the lifecycle-predicate gate. The tool reads active rows only (get_by_codes filters status='active'), so without this the assertion could pass over rows the tool is structurally unable to see — which is exactly what happened to composition_motif_link_edit for fifteen runs. Verified NOT to change the seeded value: all 84 system motifs are active today, so this tightens the assertion without moving its number.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE owner_user_id='019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c' AND code LIKE 'adopted-%'
seed_assert.why: SCOPED, not a headcount of the caller's library. That library is 152 and MOVING — the other scenarios in this batch seed into it, and my own seed-smoke added a row while I was verifying the fixture. The system side (84, owner_user_id NULL) is stable and is asserted above; here the check is simply that no ADOPTED clone exists yet, so one appearing is attributable to this turn.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a clone lands with NO confirm card (Tier W — its own description says adopting 'crosses the tenancy boundary and counts against your library quota', which is why it is human-confirmed), OR the model invents a motif_id rather than listing the built-ins first, OR it passes retag_genres the author never mentioned — retagging is optional and silently re-genre-ing an adopted motif changes what it will match later.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit — this is a cross-tenancy copy against a quota.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a motif_id that is neither public nor the caller's must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — 🔴 THIS TOOL CROSSES THE BOUNDARY BY DESIGN, so the check is the inverse of every other one in this batch: adopting a PUBLIC motif must be allowed, and adopting another USER's private motif must not.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter — the fixture's own — before anything is applied. This tool CREATES real book chapters from a previewed proposal, so the count moving is the whole signal. The card is never approved, so it must still be 1 afterwards. CONTROL: `proposal_id` comes from plan_bootstrap_propose, which has NOT been run here, so the honest outcome may be a refusal naming the missing proposal — a PRECONDITION finding rather than a tool defect.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: chapters are created with NO confirm card (Tier A — this materialises real book content), OR the model invents a proposal_id, OR the reply claims chapters were created while the card is still pending. Store check: loreweave_book.chapters stays at 1.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it creates real chapters.

scenarios.prompt: What skills do I have available?
follow_ups: Turn off the glossary skill for me.
scenarios.prompt_source: Unchanged across three arms — both previous ones lost 5 of 5 runs to transport errors, so it has never been measured. Nothing implicates the prompt.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM skills WHERE slug='glossary' AND tier='system'
seed_assert.why: The `glossary` skill exists and is System-tier. Disabling a System skill 'applies only to this user; the shared skill is never changed', so the SHARED row must be untouched, and the card is never approved so the per-user toggle must not land either. 🔴 SCOPED TO tier='system' 2026-08-23. The original counted EVERY row with this slug and expected 1; the store holds 6 — one system-tier skill and five USER-TIER copies, all created 2026-07-02 and none of them this loop's debris. A user-tier copy sharing the slug is how a per-user override works, so the count was wrong about the schema, not about the store. The assertion's own `why` says the SHARED row must be untouched, and tier='system' is exactly that row — this makes it measure what it already claimed to.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the toggle lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends enabled=true when the author said turn it OFF — a bare boolean, so an inverted value silently does the opposite while the card still reads 'set skill enabled' — OR it targets a different slug. CONTROL: disabling a System skill is PER-USER only, so a reply saying it is off 'for everyone', or warning the author they are changing a shared skill, is wrong about the blast radius in the direction that would scare them off a safe action.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 38) — an unknown slug is refused BY NAME: 'skill not found: no-such-skill-xyz'.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — disabling an already-disabled skill must be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — scope=USER: the per-user toggle must not touch another account or the shared row.
